claims.text: The baseline Hf-Mo-Ta-Ti-Zr RHEA is a single-phase BCC alloy.
The baseline Hf-Mo-Ta-Ti-Zr RHEA has high density and insufficient room-temperature ductility.
Adding 1-3 at.% Si will induce a secondary intermetallic phase in Hf-Mo-Ta-Ti-Zr.
The Si-induced intermetallic phase will consist of silicides such as MoSi2 or Ti5Si3.
The silicides will form a continuous reticulated network at grain boundaries and triple junctions.
Controlled cooling or homogenization annealing will promote formation of the proposed silicide network.
The reticulated intermetallic network will deflect, branch, or arrest propagating cracks at phase boundaries.
Crack deflection and branching will increase fracture-surface area and energy dissipation.
The proposed silicide network will improve room-temperature compressive ductility relative to the unreinforced alloy.
The Si-alloyed alloy will exceed 5% room-temperature compressive strain to failure.
Si addition and silicide formation will cause a slight or moderate increase in density.
The brittle silicide phase may reduce ultimate compressive strength.
The Si-alloyed material's yield strength may remain comparable to, or slightly below, that of a dispersion-strengthened composite.
High room-temperature friction stress of screw dislocations contributes to limited dislocation motion in the baseline alloy.
Weak B2 ordering limits dislocation motion in the single-phase BCC state.
A grain-boundary-concentrated HCP phase in HfNbTaTiZr was associated with extreme brittleness.
Isolated second-phase particles provide dispersion or second-phase strengthening rather than the proposed network-mediated crack-bridging effect.
The beneficial mechanism requires enough Si to form a percolating network but not enough to produce a fully brittle silicide-dominated structure.
The baseline alloy fails brittly because it lacks crack-deflection mechanisms.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis and predicted outcome assert a density increase, whereas the uncertainty field says the direction of the density change is uncertain because the secondary-phase volume fraction and density effect are unknown.
